newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool prices seen continuing to ease.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool prices seen continuing to ease.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to weaken further this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said in its weekly market preview.

The eastern market indicator fell by 12 cents to 605 cents a kg clean last week, while the western market indicator rose 13 cents to 572 cents a kg since the last sales in Fremantle two weeks ago. Sales this week are in Sydney and Adelaide with a total of 72,500 bales on offer.

Wesfarmers said broad wool types suffered the most last week and given the fact that a fair proportion of this week's offering consists of these, the market was expected to continue weakening. "However, it is doubtful the downturn will be too servere", Wesfarmers said.
Declining quantities for sale, due to growers responding to the fall and withdrawing much of the stock they had put back up for auction, is expected to partly counteract the situation.
Therefore, despite the current downward trend in the market, prices are not expected to revisit the lows of 1996.
